children: Yields on U.K. government bonds, or gilts, risk climbing further after hitting multi-year highs on Tuesday, says Matthew Amis, investment director at Aberdeen Investments. Renewed U.S.-Iran tensions have lifted oil prices, raising inflation risks and prospects of the Bank of England increasing interest rates in the coming months, Amis says. "Until oil and gas start freely moving in the Straits of Hormuz, gilt yields are going to struggle." Investors are also increasingly cautious ahead of Prime Minister Andy Burnham's first budget on Oct. 28 which will come amid stretched public finances, he says. Ten-year gilt yields earlier hit an 18-year high of 5.255% while 30-year gilts hit their highest since 1998 at 5.904%, LSEG data show. (miriam.mukuru@wsj.com)
